key: Uses the Antigravity CLI installed on this Mac and the Google account it is logged in with; requests count against that account's limits. Run `agy` once in Terminal to log in; `agy models` lists the model ids. Effort: low, medium, high, or max, only for a model id without its own level (a model ending in -high, -medium, or -low ignores it). Runs use agy's hearsay-notes project, whose deny rules leave the model no tools except web search, and each run's conversation is deleted from agy's history afterwards.
english: Uses the Antigravity CLI installed on this Mac and the Google account it is logged in with; requests count against that account's limits. Run `agy` once in Terminal to log in; `agy models` lists the model ids. Effort: low, medium, high, or max, only for a model id without its own level (a model ending in -high, -medium, or -low ignores it). Runs use agy's hearsay-notes project, whose deny rules leave the model no tools except web search, and each run's conversation is deleted from agy's history afterwards.

comment: Shortcut recorder hint. %d is a system error number. Windows only.

key: %@ cannot take a transcript this long on Windows: the command line would be %@ characters, and Windows allows %@. Use Claude Code, Codex, or an HTTP provider for long meetings.
english: %1$@ cannot take a transcript this long on Windows: the command line would be %2$@ characters, and Windows allows %3$@. Use Claude Code, Codex, or an HTTP provider for long meetings.
comment: Meeting notes error when the prompt would not fit on the command line (Copilot and Antigravity take it as an argument). %1$@ is a CLI name, %2$@ and %3$@ are character counts with digit grouping. Keep the product names. Windows only.

Settings > AI login status line: %1$@ is the CLI's own status output (as the CLI prints it, not translated), %2$@ the 'Run … once in Terminal to log in.' hint. The Mac joins the two the same way. Windows only.

key: Windows is running Hearsay straight from the zip file. Extract the zip to a folder you can write to, open Hearsay from there, then check for updates again.
english: Windows is running Hearsay straight from the zip file. Extract the zip to a folder you can write to, open Hearsay from there, then check for updates again.
comment: Update install error: Hearsay was opened from inside the downloaded zip file (Explorer runs it from a temporary copy). The Mac's disk image text for Windows. Windows only.

key: This copy of Hearsay is not in its own app folder, so it cannot update itself. Download the new version from the release page.
english: This copy of Hearsay is not in its own app folder, so it cannot update itself. Download the new version from the release page.
comment: Update install error: the running Hearsay.exe is not in a folder of its own. The Mac's 'not an app bundle' text for Windows. Windows only.

key: Hearsay cannot write to the folder %@. Move the Hearsay folder to a folder you can write to, open it from there, then check for updates again.
english: Hearsay cannot write to the folder %@. Move the Hearsay folder to a folder you can write to, open it from there, then check for updates again.
comment: Update install error. %@ is a folder path. The Mac's text without the Applications folder. Windows only.

key: The zip file could not be extracted: %@
english: The zip file could not be extracted: %@
comment: Update verification error. %@ is the system's error message. The Mac's disk image text for Windows. Windows only.

key: The zip file should contain one Hearsay.exe but contains %lld.
english: The zip file should contain one Hearsay.exe but contains %lld.
comment: Update verification error. %lld is a number of Hearsay.exe files. Keep Hearsay.exe. Windows only.

key: The new version is signed by %@, not by %@ like this copy of Hearsay.
english: The new version is signed by %1$@, not by %2$@ like this copy of Hearsay.
comment: Update verification error. %1$@ is the new version's certificate subject, %2$@ the running copy's (either may be 'unknown'). Windows only.

key: The new app has the product name %@, not Hearsay.
english: The new app has the product name %@, not Hearsay.
comment: Update verification error. %@ is the product name in the new Hearsay.exe (or 'none'). The Mac's bundle identifier text for Windows. Windows only.

key: The release has no Windows zip file or checksum list.
english: The release has no Windows zip file or checksum list.
comment: Update error: the GitHub release lacks the Windows download. The Mac's disk image text for Windows. Windows only.

key: The last update could not be installed. Hearsay is still the previous version.
english: The last update could not be installed. Hearsay is still the previous version.
comment: Shown after Hearsay reopens when the update helper failed to replace the app. Windows only.

key: Could not load the speech model: %@
english: Could not load the speech model: %@
comment: Transcription error when whisper.cpp cannot load the model file. %@ is the technical reason (English). Windows only (the Mac shows the decoder's error as it is).
Error detail after 'API call failed: …' or 'The download failed: …' when the server did not answer in time (the Mac shows the system's text). Windows only.
Error detail after 'The download failed: …'. %lld is an HTTP status code such as 404. Windows only.
Inserted into update errors for a version or certificate Hearsay could not read ('The new app is version unknown, not 1.2.0.'). Windows only.
Inserted into an update error when the new Hearsay.exe has no product name ('The new app has the product name none, not Hearsay.'). Windows only.
